svg.title: Connection budget of the PrestaShop database tier: pods times PHP-FPM workers times two against max_connections
svg.desc: Diagram of how many connections the Pocket Coffee cluster can open to the RDS instance pocketcoffee-prod. On the left, the web Deployment at its autoscaling maximum of six pods with twenty PHP-FPM workers each, which is one hundred and twenty workers, each of which can hold two connections, a legacy one and a Doctrine one, so up to two hundred and forty. Below it the cron pod, the release Job and monitoring add a small fixed number. These numbers are examples. On the right, a horizontal bar represents max_connections of the instance, read with SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES, for example 600: the worst case of the web pods fills forty percent of it, the fixed consumers a small part, and the rest is headroom that must stay free for failover reconnect storms, a second Deployment revision during a rolling update, and administrators. The rule printed at the bottom is that the sum of the worst cases must stay below max_connections, and that RDS Proxy is added when it does not.
svg.text: Connection math: worst case against max_connections
Example numbers for pocketcoffee-prod; read your own max_connections and measure Max_used_connections
pocketcoffee-web at the HPA maximum
6 pods x pm.max_children 20 = 120 PHP-FPM workers
Each busy worker: 1 legacy PDO connection
plus 1 Doctrine connection on Symfony pages
worst case 120 x 2 = 240
plus a slave connection per worker if replicas are configured
Fixed consumers
pocketcoffee-cron: 1 pod, a few processes
pocketcoffee-migrate Job during a release
monitoring exporter, admin sessions, RDS itself
about 30
RDS instance: max_connections = 600 (example)
web 240
headroom 330
The headroom is not waste. It absorbs:
- a failover, when every pod reconnects at once
- a rolling update with old and new pods together
- slow queries that keep connections busy longer
- people running mysql by hand
RDS Proxy pools connections when the budget cannot be met:
clients still hold 240, the database sees fewer.
Rule
(max pods x pm.max_children x connections per worker) + fixed consumers + a failover margin must stay below max_connections
